config-manager-recovery.rollback.desc: A rollback point is kept automatically at the end of every turn: a workspace snapshot plus the session cursor -- there is no manual capture form. A rewind only overwrites the workspace paths that point recorded, and deletes the paths proven to have been created after that point which pass the safety rules (.git / node_modules / the plugin data directory / oversized files are always refused; files that already existed but were passed over by the budget are in the proof list too, so they are never mistaken for new ones; nothing is removed while the proof list itself is incomplete). Session rollback forks a new child session at the stable boundary before the target turn, and the original session log stays read-only and is never rewritten.

config-manager-recovery.sessions.desc: Scans the sessions already on this machine and reports each on one of four severity levels: would block DSH startup / cannot load / next request fails / invisible. The scan itself is read-only and writes nothing. Only two classes can be repaired in-app: lossless -- replayed duplicate rows and provable synthetic closer blocks (dropping them restores the log); lossy -- seq gaps and unparsable rows (truncation; each item must be confirmed explicitly, never batched). Both go through a preview, an automatic backup and rollback. Everything else has three real destinations: (1) session layout relocation (move the unit back where its header cwd says it belongs); (2) duplicate-id quarantine (you choose which copy to keep, the rest go to a quarantine directory) -- those two can now also run right here in this panel (the "Session layout repair" entry in the sessions dialog, which runs while DSH is running and relies on the pre-write gates plus per-item rollback), as well as with the offline dcm sessions repair --fix; (3) containers or first frames that cannot be read, future formats, unregistered workspaces, and subagents without a parent -- this tool does NOT repair them (the offline CLI cannot either); they need manual handling or a DSH-side action.

config-manager-recovery.sessions.hidden.healthy: Another {count} session(s) are healthy and hidden by "show only problematic conversations".
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.danglingToolCall: Tool call without a matching result
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.duplicateId: Same session id in several workspaces
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.duplicateToolCallId: Duplicate tool-call id in one step
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.formatNewer: Session format newer than this DSH (skipped silently)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.locationMismatch: Log location does not match its workspace
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.syntheticCloser: Synthetic closer conflicts with real continuation
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.toolResultIdMismatch: Tool result id does not match its call
config-manager-recovery.sessions.issue.unregisteredWorkspace: No workspace record points at it
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.apiMissing: This client does not support layout repair (layoutRepairSessions is missing); update the plugin and retry -- nothing was changed on this machine.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.desc: Repairs the two problems that block DSH startup: a session directory that disagrees with its header cwd is moved back where it belongs (directory move only -- the first frame is not rewritten), and when one session id exists in several directories only the copy you pick is kept; the rest go to a quarantine directory (recoverable by hand).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.keepHint: The copy you pick is left untouched this round; the other copies go to the quarantine directory. Nothing can run before you choose.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.keepMissing: {count} duplicate id(s) still have no copy selected.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.keepTitle: Duplicate id: pick which copy to keep
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.kind.rewriteMove: Rewrite first frame, then move (offline CLI path)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.noCandidates: No sessions fall into this class on this machine: the scan found nothing to relocate and no duplicate ids.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.planEmpty: The plan has no action to run.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.planReadOnly: The plan is read-only: zero writes before you confirm.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.planSkipped: Another {count} item(s) are report-only (missing cwd / locked session / inconsistent cwd across generations) -- this entry does not touch them.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.planTitle: Layout repair plan (read-only, nothing changed yet)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.quarantineNote: For duplicate ids you must pick which copy to keep; the other copies are moved into a quarantine directory (.cm-repair-quarantine-*, recoverable by hand). This entry never deletes a session.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.busy: The log was written within the last 30 seconds (possibly in active use)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.duplicateId: The same session id exists in several directories
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.inconsistentGener: Generations of this session disagree on cwd (no guess is made)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.keepNotACandidate: The selected copy is not one of the scanned copies, so execution was refused
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.locked: The session directory holds a session.lock (possibly in use)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.missingKeep: No copy was selected to keep, so execution was refused (no copy was touched)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.missingTargetKey: The plan has no target projectKey; nothing was moved
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.needsRewriteMove: Needs the first-frame cwd rewritten before moving (offline CLI path)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.noCwd: The first frame has no cwd, so the target directory cannot be determined
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.notFound: The session directory or log is gone
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.quarantineExists: The quarantine directory already holds a copy with this name; nothing was moved
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.reindexFailed: Session index refresh failed (that item was rolled back)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.reindexUnavailabl: This host provides no session-index refresh, so nothing was executed (zero changes made)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.rewriteFailed: Rewriting the first-frame cwd failed, so the directory was not moved
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.sessionsRootUnrea: The sessions root could not be read, so no plan was made (zero changes made)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.reason.targetExists: The target location already holds this session; nothing was moved
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.refreshHint: The list is re-scanned after the run; failed items are rolled back individually on a best-effort basis -- any item whose rollback also failed is flagged separately and never shown as restored; retry or use the offline CLI.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.runtimeNote: This entry runs while DSH is running -- unlike the offline CLI, which requires DSH to be stopped: it relies on pre-write gates (SAFE MODE / no session.lock / not inside the write-quiescence window), a session-index refresh after every move, and a per-item rollback on failure; when the host offers no index refresh, nothing is executed at all.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.status.rollbackFailed: Failed, and the rollback did NOT succeed (needs manual handling)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.status.rolledBack: Failed, rolled back to the original state
config-manager-recovery.sessions.layout.title: Session layout repair (write action)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.noRoot: No sessions directory on this machine (no conversation yet, or DSH home is not this one).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.allDone: Repaired {ok}; {failed} not repaired (per-item reasons below; repaired rows are removed from the list).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.available: {count} session(s) can be repaired in-app; click Repair on a row to preview, or use "Repair all" to process them in order.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.desc: For classes the in-app path does not touch (invalid containers / unreadable headers / future formats ...), preview in a terminal first; close DSH before writing.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.history.title: Repair history (rollback available)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.history.unreadable: The repair ledger could not be read, so past repairs cannot be listed or rolled back here (the backup files are still in the session directory).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.none: No session can be repaired in-app this time. In-app repair covers: replayed duplicate rows / provable synthetic closer blocks (lossless), and seq gaps or unparsable rows (truncation, LOSSY, needs confirmation). Everything else is in the offline commands below.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.noneShort: No session can be repaired in-app this time.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.plan.backup: A timestamped backup is written first; after applying you can roll back from "Repair history" below.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.plan.lossy: This plan contains a LOSSY action: events after the truncation point are dropped (they cannot be recovered from the log, but the backup allows one-click rollback). Confirm before choosing "Truncate and repair".
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.plan.summary: Will drop {rows} replayed duplicate event(s) ({before} -> {after}); every other byte is preserved.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.plan.title: Repair plan: {session}
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.alreadyRolledBack: This repair has already been rolled back.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.backupInvalid: The backup is unavailable or untrusted, so the rollback was refused.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.busy: The log was written within the last 30 seconds (possibly in active use). Wait until it is quiet, then repair.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.changed: The file changed after the preview, so writing the old plan was refused. Run the check and preview again.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.corruptContainer: The container cannot be proven self-consistent (pre-write check failed) -- repair was refused rather than made more aggressive.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.invalidHeader: The first frame is not a valid single-line JSON header -- in-app repair does not rebuild headers.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.locked: The session directory holds a session.lock -- it may be in use, so the write was refused.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.lossyRequired: This session can only be repaired with a LOSSY truncation; you must confirm explicitly before it runs.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.notFound: The session log file is gone.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.nothingToFix: No losslessly repairable replayed duplicate rows were found.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.postcheckFailed: The post-write re-check failed, so the backup was restored.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.repairNotFound: No such entry in the repair ledger (it may have been pruned).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.targetChanged: The target had changed again before the rollback (fingerprint mismatch), so overwriting was refused -- newer content is never overwritten.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.tornTail: Only a torn tail frame is present (DSH truncates and heals it itself); nothing to repair.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.unavailable: This runtime has no zstd support, so repair is unavailable; use the offline CLI instead.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.unknown: The repair did not succeed (unknown reason); the original file is unchanged.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.unknownUnit: This session is no longer in the session store (it may have just been moved or deleted).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.unreadable: The log could not be read.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.verificationRefus: The pre-write check did not pass, so repair was refused.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.verifyFailed: The post-write real-codec re-check failed, so this repair was not accepted (whether it was rolled back is shown in the verification result below).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.reason.writeFailed: Writing failed (temp file / backup / swap), and the original file is unchanged.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.rejectedNext: The original file was not modified. Run the health check again for the latest state; if the reason mentions a changed file or active writing, retry once that session is quiet.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.rollbackConfirmMessage: This swaps the log of session {session} back to the pre-repair backup. If the session changed after the repair, the rollback is refused (newer content is never overwritten). Continue?
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.rolledBack: Rolled back to the pre-repair content
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.title: How to repair
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.verify.current: Re-check passed: the DSH read path can load this session right now.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.verify.migrated: Re-check passed: only the MIGRATION CHAIN can restore it (this is not the DSH live read path) -- "restorable through migration" is not "readable by the live read path".
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.verify.rollbackFailed: Dangerous state: after the re-check failed, the automatic rollback did NOT succeed; the target still holds the repaired bytes and needs manual handling.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.repair.verify.unverified: Unverified: this machine cannot run the real-codec re-check, so DSH being able to read it right now is NOT proven -- unverified is not the same as verified (that says nothing about whether the write landed).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.section.attentionNone: No session in the list needs attention.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.title: Session health check
config-manager-recovery.sessions.truncated: List truncated: {count} more not shown (run the check again or narrow the scope).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.unreadableEntries: {count} directory/file entries could not be read (counted as-is, never treated as fine).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.untested: Another {count} session(s) exceeded the scan limit and were not checked.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.unverified: {verified} deeply checked, {count} not deeply checked (unverified is not the same as healthy)
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.hint: DSH packages this session's raw log (including descendant sessions and attachments) itself; the plugin is not involved, so orphaned and multi-generation logs come along.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.reason.authRequired: The export channel could not be verified: the loopback request was rejected by authentication (status {status}). This does not mean export is unsupported here — restart DSH and try again.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.reason.networkError: No response while probing the export channel (unreachable or timed out). The entry stays enabled: if the download still fails, DSH will report the concrete reason.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.reason.readFailed: The export channel is live, but this session's log could not be read (status {status}). Repair this session above first.
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.reason.serviceMissing: The current DSH session-export channel is unavailable: the persistence backend is missing required services (session-query / session-persistence / attachments). This entry is disabled (status {status}).
config-manager-recovery.sessions.zip.reason.unexpectedStatus: The export channel returned an unexpected status ({status}). The entry stays enabled, but the download may fail.
